failure_patterns: Overall: 36 of 87 new queries correct. Non-negation queries: 10 of 16 (all 10 where 안/없/못 is glued to its word pass, all 6 where it stands as a spaced token fail). Negation queries: 26 of 71. Script and data: <scratchpad>/parser/{cases.py,run.py,judge.py,judged.json}.

P1 Whitespace-token matching (t in ('안','못'), t.startswith('않'/'없'), exact '말고'). Glued spellings real users type pass through silently and the negated concept stays in pos, which inverts the query: 모자안쓴, 모자 안쓴, 안경안쓴, 밥 안먹는, 목줄 안한, 자지않는, 목줄없이, 사람없는, 의자말고 (E1-E5, B3, C3, C4, D13; 9 cases).

P2 NP operators (말고/아닌/아니라/빼고/없-) take exactly one preceding token. A multi-word NP or a nominalized clause leaves its modifier in pos and yields junk neg: '잠든 게 아니라' -> pos keeps 잠든, neg '게 고양이'; '흑백 사진이 아닌' -> pos '흑백 고양이'; '츄르 먹는 거 말고' -> neg '거 고양이'; '교실 안이 아니라' -> pos keeps 교실; coordination '사람이나 강아지 없이' negates only 강아지 (D4, D5, D6, D10, D14, D15, C6).

P3 Negation on an auxiliary (-고 있지 않-, -어 있지 말고). scope_before stops at the main verb's connective 고, so neg becomes '있는 고양이' / '있지 고양이' (matches almost every photo) while the main verb stays in pos: '자고 있지 않은' -> pos '자고 고양이' (B4, B5, D12). The most damaging failure because the subtraction is applied to all candidates.
P4 Missing negation forms: -지 못하- (A8), -지도/-지는 않- with an intervening particle (B6), and -지 말고 handled by the noun rule, which outputs the raw -지 form ('자지 고양이', a vulgar homograph) (D11, D12).

P5 Wearing detection by surface prefix (WEAR_HEADS includes 하/했/차/매/쓰). Light verbs and homographs become '착용': '그루밍을 착용한', '목욕을 착용한', '산책을 착용한', '공을 착용한' (차다 = kick), '나무에를 착용한' (매달리다, and strip_particle lacks 에), '우산을 착용한' (쓰다 = use) (A2, A3, A4, A5, B7, F6).

P6 adnominal() decides 'already adnominal' from the final batchim after stripping the connective 고, so ㄹ/ㄴ-final stems break: 놀고 -> '놀 고양이', 울고 -> '울 고양이', 안고 -> '학생이 안 고양이' (G2, A13, A14). -게 adverbs get 는 appended: '예쁘게는 고양이', '생기게는 고양이' (J2, J3).

P7 Leftward scope of 안/못/-지 않- runs to the clause start and swallows positive setting adverbials: '풀밭에 눈을 안 감고 앉은' -> neg '풀밭에 눈을 감는 고양이', pos loses 풀밭; '햇빛 아래 눈 안 뜬' loses 햇빛 아래 (A11, A12). It stops at -에서 only by accident, because 서 is in CONNECTIVE (A9).

P8 No head-noun check. A negated relative clause that modifies a person is turned into a cat negative and the person attribute is dropped: '안경을 안 쓰신 선생님과', '모자 안 쓴 사람이랑', '웃지 않는 사람 품에', '우산 안 쓴 학생 옆' (F1, F3, F4, F6). Cat as object breaks pos: '고양이를 학생들' (F5).

P9 Lexicalized words typed with a space are read as negation: N+없- adjectives/adverbs ('쉴 새 없이' -> '새(bird)와 함께 있는 고양이', '어이 없는', '힘 없이', '할 일 없는'), '못 생기게', and 안 = inside ('상자 안 슈딩이' -> neg '상자 고양이는 고양이') (C7-C10, J1, J2). K6 '없어진' passes only because it is the first token.

P10 Neg template chosen by the particle, not by what the noun is: 이/가 -> '에 있는' even for people and 혼자 ('선생님에 있는 고양이', '혼자에 있는 고양이'); otherwise a bare compound ('사람 고양이', '책상 고양이'). Quantifiers 아무도/아무것도 are not resolved ('아무와 함께', '아무것을 착용한'). The honorific existential 계시다 is not mapped to 있다 (D7, D8, D9, C5, G8, F2; D1/H4 minor).

P11 Name normalization covers only the exact string 슈딩이: '슈딩', '냥이' pass through (I3, I2). Replacing the name with 고양이 also erases contrasts with other cats: '검은 고양이 말고 슈딩이' -> neg '고양이에 있는 고양이' (D14).

P12 Cosmetic leftovers in pos with no condition lost: orphan auxiliaries and connectives ('있는', '있었던', '있는데', '앉아서') and orphan head nouns ('곳에서', '곳의') (A6, A9, A10, C1, D2, G5, G6, H4). They add noise to the embedding but were not counted as failures.
general_fixes: F1 Detect negation on morphemes, not whitespace tokens. Run Kiwi (kiwipiepy, pip, CPU only); it also repairs spacing. Read negation from POS tags: 안/MAG, 못/MAG, 않/VX, 못하/VX, 말/VX after -지, 없/VA, 아니/VCN, plus the exceptive particles 말고/빼고. One rule then covers glued and spaced forms and tells apart 안/NNG (inside), 안경/NNG, 안기/VV, 편안/XR and 못생기/VA. If no dependency is allowed, split X안Y / X못Y / X없Y only when X is a noun and Y is a conjugated predicate (it ends in a verbal ending), never when XY or 안Y is a dictionary noun.

F2 Use a closed inventory of negation constructions, each an operator over a predicate or over an NP: (a) short form 안/못 + PRED; (b) long form PRED-지 (도|는|를|가)? (않|못하|말); (c) existential NP (이|가|도|은|는)? 없-; (d) copular NP (이|가)? 아니-(ㄴ|라|고); (e) exceptive NP 말고/빼고/제외하고. -지 말고 belongs to (b), not to the NP rule.

F3 Treat main verb + auxiliary (-고 있-, -어 있-, -고 싶-, -어 보-) as one predicate before applying negation. Negation on the auxiliary scopes over the whole unit, so '자고 있지 않은' gives neg '자고 있는 고양이'. When the main verb moves to neg, its auxiliary goes with it, so no orphan '있는' is left in pos.

F4 Scope for short and long negation = the predicate plus its internal arguments: the nearest 을/를-marked or bare object noun, and a locative only when the verb subcategorizes for one (motion/position verbs such as 나가다, 올라가다, 들어가다, 눕다, 앉다, 있다, 매달리다). Free adverbials (N에서, N 아래/위/옆에 with a non-locative verb, time words, manner adverbs) stay in pos. Stop at the first case-marked phrase the verb does not license, and drop the accidental dependence on 서 in CONNECTIVE.

F5 Scope for NP operators = the whole NP chunk on the left: adnominal modifiers (-ㄴ/-은/-는/-던), adjectives, N의 N, N + 안/위/옆, and a nominalized clause (-ㄴ/는 것/거/게) as one unit. Distribute the operator over coordinated NPs (A(이)나 / 랑 / 와·과 / 하고 B).

F6 Head-noun rule: an adnominal predicate modifies the next noun. If that noun is not the cat (고양이, the name, an alias, 얘/쟤), the negation is part of that noun's description, so keep the clause in pos (or drop it) and emit no cat negative. If the cat carries the object marker (고양이를/을), the negated predicate describes another agent.

F7 Pick the neg template from the semantic class of the excluded thing, not from its particle: person/animal -> 'N과 함께 있는 고양이' (or 'N이 V는 고양이' for agentive verbs such as 안다); place -> 'N에 있는 고양이'; clothing/accessory -> wearing template; action or clause -> 'clause + 고양이'. A few lexical items need their own handling: 혼자가 아닌 flips (pos 'with someone', neg '혼자 있는 고양이'), 아무도 -> 사람, 아무것도 + 입다 -> 옷.

F8 Detect wearing from (noun class, verb lemma) pairs, not surface prefixes: 쓰다 with headwear/eyewear/masks, 입다 with clothes, 신다 with footwear, 끼다 with glasses/gloves/rings, 차다 with watches/belts/collars, 매다 with ties/ribbons, 하다 with accessory nouns (목도리, 목줄, 리본, 넥타이, 목걸이). Lemmatize first (했->하다, 썼->쓰다, 찼->차다). Any other N + 하다 is a light verb -> 'N하는 고양이'.

F9 Build adnominals from the lemma: action verbs take present -는, with ㄹ deletion (놀다->노는, 울다->우는) and ㄴ-final stems kept (안다->안는). Resultative state verbs take past -ㄴ/은 (눈을 감다->감은, 앉다->앉은, 잠들다->잠든). Check for an existing adnominal only on the original surface ending, never after a connective was stripped. Under negation, a -게 adverb goes to neg together with the verb it modifies ('안 예쁘게 나온' -> neg '예쁘게 나온 고양이').
F10 Map honorific lemmas before classification: 계시다->있다, 주무시다->자다, 드시다/잡수시다->먹다; strip -시- from other verbs.

F11 Keep an exception lexicon of standard-dictionary single words and match it with spaces removed: N+없다 adjectives/adverbs (어이없다, 힘없다, 정신없다, 재미없다, 상관없다, 끝없다, 틀림없다, 쉴새없이, 할일없다), 못+V lexemes (못생기다, 못되다, 못나다), and 안 as a noun after container/space nouns or before a particle or noun (상자 안, 가방 안에). These are dictionary facts, not benchmark tuning.

F12 Normalize aliases with a pattern (슈딩, 슈딩이, 슈딩아 plus particles) and generic forms (냥이, 냥). When the query contrasts the name with other cats, send the other cat to neg as '다른 고양이' instead of collapsing both into 고양이.

F13 Sanity-check the output. Drop a neg phrase whose only content is 고양이 plus a generic predicate (있는/하는/있지), or that contains 고양이 twice, since subtracting it hurts every candidate. In pos, convert leftover connective endings to adnominal form (-는데/-고/-서/-며; this generalizes the existing 지만->는 rule) and remove orphan head nouns (곳/데) whose modifier was negated.

F14 Turn this stress set into parser unit tests kept outside bench/, so the parser can improve without touching the frozen dev/test queries. Failures most likely to cost retrieval quality, in order: P3 (degenerate '있는 고양이' negative), P1 and P2 (polarity inversions), then P8 (false cat negatives from clauses about people).
